posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
All the physics info on reflection from two different index of refraction mediums all has to do with a distinct line between the two materials with different index of refractions. Like glass and air, oil and water etc...

But I have not seen where the two index of refractions don't have a fine line of distinction but a fuzzy line where the two merge as in the fringes made by a reflection phase hologram (constructive and destructive fringes in an interference pattern do not go from black to white, but rather black, different grays, white). How does this affect the reflection of light compared to the distince line reflection?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: I guess where two different index of refraction materials meet is the Bragg Plane, right? But what I am asking is how this works when the Bragg plane is fuzzy, not well defined?
